review.translation: [I have set|2] [my rainbow|1,0] [in the clouds|3], [and it will be|4] [the sign of|5] [the covenant|6] [between me|7] [and|8] [the earth|9].

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Correct the occurrence’s root assignment from קשש to קשת and link it to the existing rainbow sense of קֶשֶׁת at word index 0.
draft.definition: A rainbow, the bow visible in the clouds.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:13 identifies the bow in the cloud as the sign of God's covenant with the earth. The existing קשת article cites this verse under the rainbow sense of קֶשֶׁת.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks קַשְׁתִּי as the object of נָתַתִּי, “I have set.” God sets his bow בֶּעָנָן, “in the cloud,” and calls it לְאוֹת בְּרִית, “a sign of the covenant.” Its location identifies the bow as a rainbow.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a first-person singular possessive suffix, “my.” The ת belongs to the noun קֶשֶׁת.

analysis.evidence: אֶת־קַשְׁתִּי marks “my bow” as the direct object, and בֶּעָנָן specifies where God has set it, “in the cloud.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular. The ending ־תִּי marks the subject “I.”
analysis.sense: put or set something in a place

analysis.evidence: In אֶת קַשְׁתִּי נָתַתִּי בֶּעָנָן, God places his bow in the cloud. The cloud is where the bow appears, and the bow serves as the sign of the covenant.
analysis.morphology: בֶּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article before עָנָן, a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: After נָתַתִּי, “I have set,” וְהָיְתָה לְאוֹת בְּרִית states what the bow will serve as. The לְ in לְאוֹת marks its role as a sign of the covenant between God and the earth.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes the Qal perfect third-person feminine singular. The verb agrees with קַשְׁתִּי, “my bow,” and has future force here.

analysis.evidence: God sets his bow in the cloud and says וְהָיְתָה לְאוֹת בְּרִית, “and it shall serve as a sign of the covenant.” The bow is the visible sign of the covenant between God and the earth.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks the role the bow will serve. אוֹת is a common noun of common gender, singular in the construct state, linked to בְּרִית.

analysis.evidence: God sets his bow in the cloud as the sign of a covenant described as בֵּינִי וּבֵין הָאָרֶץ, “between me and the earth.” The bow identifies this as the covenant with Noah and all flesh.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase לְאוֹת בְּרִית, “as a sign of a covenant.”
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.evidence: In בְּרִית בֵּינִי וּבֵין הָאָרֶץ, “a covenant between me and the earth,” the suffix on בֵּינִי identifies God as the first party, and וּבֵין הָאָרֶץ introduces the earth as the second.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with a first-person common singular pronominal suffix referring to God, the speaker.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In בְּרִית בֵּינִי וּבֵין הָאָרֶץ, ‘a covenant between me and the earth’, וּבֵין introduces the earth as the second party to the covenant.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ is prefixed to the preposition בֵין ‘between’.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: בֵּינִי וּבֵין הָאָרֶץ means “between me and the earth.” The bow in the cloud marks a covenant whose scope is the earth as a whole.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. The noun has the pausal form אָרֶץ at the end of the verse.
